Executive Overview

This report analyzes 1,465 Amazon India products across 4 top-level categories, examining pricing dynamics, discount patterns, and customer satisfaction signals. The dataset captures real-time catalog data including list prices, selling prices, discount percentages, customer ratings, and review volumes.

Pricing & Discount Strategy Analysis

This is the most critical section of the report. We examine whether discount depth translates into higher customer satisfaction, and how pricing tiers influence ratings and engagement.

Critical Finding: The correlation between discount percentage and customer rating is -0.155 — essentially negligible. Deep discounts do not meaningfully predict higher satisfaction. This means aggressive discounting is likely eroding margin without commensurate customer experience gains.
Finding: The correlation between discount percentage and review volume is 0.011 — also weak. Heavily discounted products do not consistently attract more reviews. Review volume appears driven more by category popularity and product type than by promotional intensity.
Interpretation: The correlation matrix confirms that pricing and discount variables have very weak linear relationships with ratings. The strongest signal is between actual price and discounted price (expected). Rating count shows mild positive correlation with higher discount percentages, but the relationship is modest.

Customer Engagement & Rating Distribution

Understanding how ratings and review volumes are distributed reveals patterns in customer engagement and product quality signals across the catalog.

Finding: The rating distribution is left-skewed toward higher ratings — the majority of products cluster between 3.5★ and 4.5★. The mean rating count (18,307) is significantly higher than the median (5,179), indicating a power-law distribution where a small number of products attract disproportionate review volume.

Review Sentiment Snapshot

We analyzed 11,955 review titles across all products using keyword-based sentiment classification to understand the voice of the customer at a catalog level.

Finding: Review sentiment is predominantly positive, with the most frequent words being "quality," "value," "working," "fast," and "worth" — indicating customers primarily evaluate products on build quality, value for money, and functional reliability.
Negative Themes: Common complaints center on durability ("stopped working," "broke"), authenticity concerns ("fake," "not original"), and quality inconsistency ("defective," "damaged"). These themes appear across multiple categories and represent systemic quality assurance opportunities.

Strategic Recommendations

Based on the data analysis above, here are five actionable recommendations for category managers and pricing strategists. Each recommendation is grounded in specific data points from this report.

1. Recalibrate Discount Strategy — Depth Doesn't Drive Satisfaction

The correlation between discount percentage and rating is just -0.155, indicating no meaningful linear relationship. Aggressive discounts (>60%) do not produce higher-rated products. Instead of blanket deep discounts, focus promotional dollars on strategic price anchoring (showing value through moderate discounts of 20-40%) and invest the margin saved into product quality improvements.

Discount-Rating r = -0.155 Avg discount: 48%

2. Prioritize Category-Level Quality Interventions

The bottom-performing categories by rating (Home&Kitchen at 4.04★) need targeted assortment review. Consider raising the bar on product inclusion criteria for these categories — minimum rating thresholds, stricter seller vetting, or curated sub-category pages that surface higher-quality alternatives. The opportunity matrix above highlights which categories offer the highest ROI for quality improvement.

Bottom category: 4.04★ Top category: 4.31★

3. Leverage High-Engagement Products as Category Anchors

Review volume follows a power-law distribution — a small set of products capture disproportionate attention. Identify the top-reviewed products in each category and use them as category anchors in navigation and search results. These products have proven customer trust and can drive category-level conversion rates.

Median reviews: 5,179 Mean reviews: 18,307

4. Address the Catalog's "Long Tail" Quality Problem

While 76% of products score 4.0★+, roughly 0.4% fall below 3.0★. These low-rated products damage overall catalog perception. Implement a systematic review process for sub-3.0★ products: flag for supplier review, request product improvements, or consider delisting chronically poor performers, particularly in high-visibility categories.

Sub-3.0★: 0.4% 4.0★+: 76%

5. Invest in Authenticity & Durability Signals

Sentiment analysis reveals that "fake," "durability," and "stopped working" are persistent negative themes across categories. Strengthen seller verification processes and consider introducing enhanced "Authenticity Guarantee" or "Durability Tested" badges for qualifying products. These signals directly address the top customer anxieties surfaced in review data.

Top complaint themes: authenticity, durability 3.1% negative sentiment in titles
